# Behaviours reproduced knowing they are wrong, because the committed corpus
# already round-tripped through them. A test that pins one of these names this
# file rather than restating the rationale, so a future contributor reads the
# reason before "fixing" the behaviour and silently reclassifying every synced
# item.
#
# quirk <name>
#   source: <bash location>
#   what:   <the behaviour>
#   why:    <why it is preserved>

quirk narrow-table-guard
  source: jira-md-tokenise.awk:78-79
  what:   a line is only rejected as a table when it BOTH starts with `|` and
          ends with `|` (optional trailing space). `| a | b` is not rejected and
          becomes paragraph text.
  why:    widening the guard would start refusing bodies that convert today.

quirk nested-list-guard-has-no-space-requirement
  source: jira-md-tokenise.awk:85-86
  what:   any indented line whose first non-space character is -, * or +, or is
          a digit run followed by `.`, is rejected as a nested list. An indented
          continuation line such as `  -word` therefore falsely rejects.
  why:    narrowing it would accept bodies the bash rejects, so a create that
          fails today would start succeeding with a different shape.

quirk listitem-second-child-dropped
  source: jira-adf-render.jq:50-51
  what:   a listItem renders `.content[0].content` only. A second paragraph, or
          a nested list under the same item, is dropped with no placeholder.
  why:    the rendered form feeds remote_hash; emitting the dropped content
          would reclassify every item carrying it.

quirk nested-list-as-first-child-renders-inline-placeholders
  source: jira-adf-render.jq:50-51
  what:   when a listItem's FIRST child is a list, its list items are fed to
          render_inline, so each yields `[unsupported ADF inline: listItem]`.
  why:    a consequence of the same expression as the quirk above; the two
          shapes genuinely differ and both are reproduced.

quirk codeblock-first-child-only
  source: jira-adf-render.jq:72-75
  what:   a codeBlock renders `.content[0].text` only; later text children are
          dropped.
  why:    same reason as listitem-second-child-dropped.

quirk ordered-list-order-always-one
  source: jira-md-assemble.jq:79
  what:   assemble always emits `attrs.order: 1`, whatever number the markdown
          used, while render honours `attrs.order // 1`. `3. three` becomes
          order 1 and renders back as `1. three`.
  why:    the round trip is not injective by design; changing it would rewrite
          every ordered list on the next sync.

quirk marks-ignored-without-a-placeholder
  source: jira-adf-render.jq:27-40
  what:   strike, underline, subsup, textColor and every other mark outside the
          code/em/strong/link pipeline are dropped silently — the text renders
          bare, with no placeholder and no warning.
  why:    a placeholder would change the rendered bytes for every item using
          them.

quirk unbalanced-emphasis-becomes-an-empty-marked-node
  source: jira-md-assemble.jq:26,44
  what:   `a*b` yields THREE text nodes, and the middle one is an em-marked
          EMPTY string rather than a literal `*`: the catch-all matches the
          single `*`, the classifier sees a leading `*`, and stripping one
          delimiter from each end of a one-character token leaves nothing.
  why:    discovered by running the oracle, not by reading it; a hand-written
          fixture would have asserted a literal asterisk.

quirk empty-link-text-is-dropped
  source: jira-md-assemble.jq:44-48
  what:   `[](https://x)` matches the link token but the assembler's capture
          requires a non-empty label, so the token contributes NOTHING to the
          document — neither a link nor text.
  why:    same as above: observed, not read.

quirk no-text-escaping
  source: jira-adf-render.jq:27-40
  what:   a literal *, _, `, [, # or | in ADF text is emitted bare, so the
          markdown it produces does not re-parse to the same ADF.
  why:    escaping would change the rendered bytes of every item.

quirk hard-break-only-in-a-paragraph
  source: jira-md-tokenise.awk:142
  what:   two or more trailing spaces are a hard break in a paragraph only. On
          a heading or a list item they are retained inside the text.
  why:    faithful to where the awk applies the rule.
